pieces.hook:
things nobody tells you
about applying online

slides.heading:
a job posting is
the longest shot
slides.body:
In a study of 4M+ candidates,
1 in 152 who applied through
a posting got hired.

slides.heading: a referral changes the odds
slides.body:
Referred candidates in the same study:
1 in 16. Almost ten times better.

slides.heading:
most jobs come
through people
slides.body:
54% of US workers say a connection
got them their job
(MyPerfectResume survey, 2025).

slides.heading:
start with people you
share something with
slides.body:
Someone from your school or your old job
is the easiest first message.

pieces.ig_caption:
things nobody tells you about applying online

Applying through a job posting is the longest shot. In Lever's study of 4M+ candidates, 1 in 152 who applied that way got hired, against 1 in 16 for referred candidates. (via SHRM, 2016)
Start with people you already share something with: your school, your old job.
pieces.tt_tease: things nobody tells you about applying online

lines:
what you needed was
one person inside
pieces.ig_caption:
paying for Premium and still hearing nothing back

LinkedIn Premium can cost $50+ a month, depending on the plan (prices vary by plan and person).
Before paying for more tools, look at how people actually get in: 54% of US workers say a connection got them their job. (MyPerfectResume survey, 2025)
pieces.tt_tease: paying for Premium and still sending cold applications?

lines:
nobody tells you the people
who can refer you
went to your school
pieces.ig_caption:
the easiest person to reach is someone from your school

Alumni at the company you want already share something with you.
Keep the first note short: what you share, who you are, and one question about how they got in.
pieces.tt_tease: your school's alumni are the easiest place to start

lines:
you: finally find
the perfect job posting

also you: one of hundreds
applying to the same one
pieces.ig_caption:
the perfect posting, and hundreds of other people found it too

Online, you're one application in a stack. Through a person, you're a name someone recognizes.
In Lever's study of 4M+ candidates, referred candidates were hired at almost ten times the rate of people applying through a posting. (via SHRM, 2016)
pieces.tt_tease: found the perfect job posting... so did everyone else

pieces.hook:
what to write to
someone you've never met

slides.heading: line 1: what you share
slides.body:
"Hi [name], I saw we both
went to [school]."

slides.heading: line 3: one small ask
slides.body:
"Would you be open to a quick call
about how you got there?"

slides.heading: then stop
slides.body:
Keep it short.
Ask about their path, not for a job.

pieces.ig_caption:
what to write to someone you've never met

Three lines is enough: what you share, who you are, one small ask.
Ask how they got there, not for a job. A referral can come later, once you've talked.
pieces.tt_tease: save this for the next time you message a stranger about a job

the scariest email this Halloween 🎃

"We've decided to move forward with other candidates." If it keeps landing after every online application, it's not just you.

lines:
POV: you spent hours
on a cover letter
nobody will read
pieces.ig_caption:
hours on a cover letter, and no one on the other end

Tailoring every application takes hours, and you often hear nothing back.
A short note to someone at the company puts your name in front of an actual person.
